question: Does a pull request's `lastEditedAt` move when its description is edited, and not when only its title is, or when its head is pushed; and does an edit by a bot or an App move it?
pass: Written 2026-11-10T20:45:57Z, before anything runs (issue 549, raised by the Claude security read of pull request 548; the leg of P-58 that decision 0140 assumed and no trial recorded). On a new canary pull request opened by the Maintainer's login, the description is edited twice by that login, and the query the facts port sends, adapters/edits.py's QUERY word for word with its variables, is read by the Maintainer's login. The Maintainer then deletes one revision from the description's edit history in the browser, by hand, and the same query is read again. Pass if the read after the deletion is answered 200 with no errors and in the shape the port reads: every node of userContentEdits, the deleted revision's among them if it is still listed, with an editedAt that is a UTC time to the second, a totalCount no less than the nodes listed, and lastEditedAt and the count agreeing that the description was edited; and if the time the port gives for it, the later of lastEditedAt and every editedAt, is no earlier than the time it gave before the deletion. Then a deleted revision still counts, as decision 0140 assumed. Fail otherwise: a deleted node whose editedAt is null or absent, or any answer the port refuses, leaves that pull request refused on every pass, and a time that moved back hides an edit; either is told to the Maintainer, and a rule and its test are owed. Recorded, deciding nothing: whether the deleted revision's node stays in the list, what its deletedAt says, and whether totalCount, lastEditedAt or editor move at the deletion. Not asked here: the same read through the reader App's token, whose key is the Maintainer's; trials/P-58.reader.json found the reader answered as the Maintainer's login is. Run on 2026-11-10 on canary pull request 101, opened and its description edited twice by the Maintainer's login (writes not recorded here), and one revision deleted by the Maintainer in the browser; ran_at is the time of the trial branch's one commit, the first write GitHub timed. Passed. Four reads are recorded for it, each answered 200 with no errors, each timed here by its answer's date. At once after it opened, cubic had already edited, nine seconds after the opening: two edits, the opening text's, editedAt 20:46:33Z with cubic's time, 20:46:42Z, as its createdAt, and cubic's. After the Maintainer's two edits, at 20:47:01Z and 20:47:06Z: four edits, lastEditedAt 20:47:06Z, editor don-petry. At 20:51:34Z, before the deletion, after CodeRabbit's edit at 20:48:14Z: five edits, lastEditedAt 20:48:14Z, editor coderabbitai, every deletedAt null. At 23:02:56Z, after the Maintainer deleted the revision of 20:47:01Z: that revision's node is still listed, in its place, its editedAt, createdAt and editor as before, and its deletedAt now 2026-11-10T23:02:37Z; every other node is as it was, totalCount is still 5 with no next page, and lastEditedAt and editor did not move. The port gives 2026-11-10T20:48:14Z for the read before the deletion and for the read after it. So a deleted middle revision keeps its time and is still listed, and its deletion moved no time: lastEditedAt, GitHub's own, stayed at the edit before it. Two later edits stood above the revision deleted, so the port's time could not have moved back whatever GitHub did with it: this leg shows the shape the port is answered for a middle revision, and nothing of the newest edit's deletion. The newest revision's leg, written 2026-11-10T23:13:41Z, before it ran, on the Claude security read of pull request 726: the middle revision's deletion could not have moved the port's time back whatever GitHub did, since two later edits stood above it. On the same pull request, by then closed, the Maintainer's login edits the description once more, so that edit is the newest and alone carries the latest time; the query is read; the Maintainer deletes that newest revision from the history by hand, if GitHub offers it; and the query is read again. Pass if the answer after it is still 200 with no errors, in the shape the port reads, and the time the port gives is no earlier than before the deletion, so an edit made after an approval is not hidden by deleting its revision. Fail if the time moves back, or the port refuses the answer. If GitHub offers no deletion of the newest revision, that is recorded on the Maintainer's word, no exchange showing it, and this leg neither passes nor fails: a newest edit then cannot be deleted while it is the newest, and one made a middle one by a later edit is the case already recorded, the later edit itself counting. Run on the same pull request. The Maintainer's login edited the description at 23:13:57Z, and the read at 23:14:10Z, the fifth exchange, shows it, on a closed pull request: six edits, lastEditedAt 23:13:57Z, editor don-petry, the revision deleted before still listed with its deletedAt. The Maintainer then looked in the browser's history for the deletion of that newest revision, and GitHub offered none: recorded on his word, no exchange showing it. So this leg neither passed nor failed, and the verdict is the first leg's. What the two give together, the second on his word alone: the browser deletes a revision only once a later edit stands above it; that later edit counts itself; and the deleted one stays listed with its time. Whether anything but the browser deletes a revision, the newest among them, was not asked.
